title: Secrets Manager and Parameter Store: two answers at different prices

videos.script: A password written into the code is in every copy of the repository, every image, and every laptop that ever cloned it. {{code}} AWS has two places to keep it instead. Parameter Store, free, for configuration by path. Secrets Manager, forty cents a secret, for credentials that should change. {{stores}} You will store a value in each, read it back, and see versions and stages: current, previous, and pending. {{stages}} You will see how rotation works: four steps, and the stage moves last. Then what moto does instead, which is the one bug a rotation must not have. {{rotation}} You will read a secret from Python and keep it for five minutes. That cache is the difference between two hundred and fifty dollars a month and less than one. {{cache}} And you will restart moto so that it checks policies. One user may read one secret, one may read all of them. Then you will see exactly what moto checks, and what it does not. {{access}}
